title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: Quarto — king implants rebellion then imputes and strips virtues
pass_a_gloss: Fourth: suppose a king so powerful he could inject into his subjects, if he wished, a spirit of rebellion and disobedience—would a wise, just, good king first impute the rebels' crime to those otherwise faithful in that city, then punish it by stripping them of justice, fidelity, and the other virtues so they thereafter could not but be rebels and criminals themselves?
pass_b_english: Fourth, suppose there is some King endowed with such power that he can, if he wishes, inject into his subjects a spirit of rebellion and disobedience. Do you think that if he is wise, if just, if good, he would be so disposed that to those who would otherwise be faithful in that city he would first impute the crime of rebels, then, to punish it, strip them of justice and fidelity and the other virtues, so that thereafter they could not but be themselves rebels and criminals?
source_text: Quarto, fac esse aliquem Regem ea potentia praeditum, ut possit subditis suis, si velit, animum rebellionis & inobedientiae immittere, putasne eum si sapiens, si justus, si bonus sit, ita fore comparatum, ut iis qui alioqui in urbe illa fideles essent, primum imputet rebellium crimen, deinde ut illud puniat eos privet justitia & fidelitate, ac caeteris virtutibus, ut deinceps non possint non esse ipsi rebelles & scelesti?
